critical_code_review_comments: rides.py/accept_ride references driver.get('user_name')/('user_phone') but the driver doc doesn't have these keys — resolves to None; driver_name/phone fall back to user.get('name'/'phone'). Minor but consider consolidating source of truth.

_ensure_driver_stats inside accept_ride updates `driver` locally but then does a SECOND update_one that overrides points but does NOT set the initial_points default if driver was brand new. Current implementation is safe because _ensure_driver_stats persists defaults first, but worth noting the two-step write.
routes/rides.py imports routes.drivers helpers inside the handler (lazy import to avoid circular imports) — OK but flags a coupling that could be refactored into a shared `services/points.py` module.

/api/drivers/my-activity caps points at 100 in ride hooks (min(100, ...)). The max_points in palette 'Expert' is also 100, so this is consistent. If palettes are ever reconfigured >100, the cap will prevent palette progression.
Driver UI login uses phone+OTP (not email/password), so the UI e2e check for /chauffeur/profile had to be verified via code + backend API, not a full UI walkthrough.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (admin UI visually verified; driver profile verified via code + API)
